samples.summary: Cross-provider account takeover: the GitHub side has no verified-email check, and this change makes email the shared identity across two providers
samples.evidence: This change makes `findOrCreateUser` (packages/backend/src/user/user.service.ts:41, matches on `email` alone) the merge point for two providers. `GoogleStrategy.validate` carefully refuses an unverified address (google.strategy.ts:81), and the diff's own docs assert the GitHub side needs no equivalent because "on the `user:email` scope it returns only addresses it has verified" (google.strategy.ts:19-20, docs/design/backend.md:896-903). Nothing in this repo enforces that: `GitHubStrategy.validate` takes `emails?.[0]?.value` (github.strategy.ts:77) with no `verified` filter, and GitHub's `/user/emails` returns *unverified* addresses too (each entry carries a `verified` flag that is never read here). `github.strategy.spec.ts` only asserts endpoint URLs, never verification. Attack: attacker adds the victim's Google address to their own GitHub account (unverified — they cannot verify it), signs in via `GET /auth/github`, and if that address lands at `emails[0]` the callback calls `findOrCreateUser({email: victim@…})` (auth.controller.ts:126) and issues a session for the victim's Google-created Wafflebase account. Before this change the same weakness only merged GitHub↔GitHub; this change extends the blast radius to every Google-created account and simultaneously documents the assumption as safe. The mitigation the Google side has (`verified === true`) is absent on the GitHub side.
searchedFor: glob for node_modules/passport-github2/**/strategy.js (not installed, could not confirm library filtering)

samples.summary: `isSecureCookie()` still reads only `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL`; a deployment that states its https scheme via the new required `GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL` gets non-`Secure`, non-`__Host-` session and state cookies
samples.evidence: `isSecureCookie()` (oauth-state.ts:229-240) decides `Secure` and the `__Host-` prefix for the session, refresh, oauth-state, cli-state and login-return cookies from `COOKIE_SECURE`, then `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL`, then `NODE_ENV`. This change introduces `GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL`, which `oauth-providers.ts:21` makes *mandatory* for Google and which states the deployment's public scheme just as GitHub's does — but it is never consulted. `github-auth.guard.ts:66-72` documents that an install with **no** `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` is a supported working deployment (GitHub falls back to the URL registered on the OAuth app). So an https install that sets `GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL=https://app.example.com/auth/google/callback`, omits `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL`, and does not set `NODE_ENV=production` falls through to line 239 and issues every login cookie without `Secure` and without the `__Host-` prefix. That is exactly the write-restriction the module says is the only thing stopping sibling-subdomain cookie tossing of the double-submit secret and of `wafflebase_session` (oauth-state.ts:26-47, 66-84) — i.e. session fixation. Adding a second callback URL without teaching `isSecureCookie()` about it leaves a configuration that looks fully specified but silently downgrades the cookies.

samples.summary: `googleAuthConfigured()` is evaluated at module-import time, before `ConfigModule.forRoot()` loads `.env` — the guard's configured-check can pass on a route whose strategy was never registered (unauthenticated 500)
samples.evidence: `const googleProviders = googleAuthConfigured() ? [GoogleStrategy] : []` runs in auth.module.ts's module body, which CommonJS evaluates while app.module.ts is still resolving its `import { AuthModule }` at app.module.ts:6 — i.e. *before* `ConfigModule.forRoot()` (app.module.ts:29) runs dotenv and assigns the `.env` file into `process.env`. `oauth-providers.ts:25` reads `process.env` directly. For the documented deployment shape that puts `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET/CALLBACK_URL` in a `.env` file (packages/backend/README.md:41-60), the strategy is therefore NOT registered, while `GoogleAuthGuard.canActivate`'s `assertGoogleConfigured()` (google-auth.guard.ts:22, evaluated per-request, after dotenv) returns true and falls through to `super.canActivate` — producing precisely the passport "Unknown authentication strategy" 500 the guard exists to prevent, on an unauthenticated URL any visitor can type. `GET /auth/providers` (auth.controller.ts:240) likewise advertises `google: true`, so the login page renders a button that leads straight to that 500. Every other env read in this module (`oauth-state.ts`, `github-auth.guard.ts`) happens at request time, so this is the one load-time read and the two answers can disagree.
searchedFor: read packages/backend/src/app.module.ts import order and ConfigModule.forRoot
read packages/backend/src/main.ts for any earlier dotenv call

samples.summary: Google callback short-circuits before `consumeWebOAuthState`, so a non-web `state` leaves the live state cookie uncleared — contradicting the helper's documented "cleared whether or not it matches"
samples.evidence: `if (typeof stateToken !== 'string' || !isWebOAuthState(stateToken) || !consumeWebOAuthState(req, res, stateToken))` (auth.controller.ts:265-271) evaluates left-to-right, so when `state` is absent, an array, garbage, or a CLI token, `consumeWebOAuthState` is never called and `__Host-wafflebase_oauth_state` is never cleared. `web-oauth-login.ts:60-61` states the opposite invariant ("The cookie is cleared whether or not it matches, so a failed login leaves nothing behind to replay"), and the new test at auth.controller.spec.ts only asserts `res.cookie` was not called, never `res.clearCookie`. Effect: an attacker who can make the victim's browser hit `/auth/google/callback?state=<junk>` (a trivial cross-site top-level navigation; the route is unauthenticated) burns nothing, and the victim's still-valid 10-minute state secret stays in the browser for the full window rather than being invalidated on a refused callback. Low impact on its own — the attacker never learns the secret — but it removes the single-use property the helper claims.
searchedFor: read the new googleAuthCallback refusal tests in auth.controller.spec.ts

samples.summary: The GitHub callback still upserts the user (and a workspace) before its `state` check, unlike the new Google callback
samples.evidence: `githubAuthCallback` calls `this.userService.findOrCreateUser(...)` at auth.controller.ts:126, *before* the `state` validation at lines 155-166; `findOrCreateUser` also creates a Workspace and a WorkspaceMember row (user.service.ts:50-66). The new Google callback deliberately inverts this (auth.controller.ts:263-271, and the diff's own comment and docs/design/backend.md:134 call it out: "a refused callback leaves no row (and no workspace) behind"). The GitHub path was not moved onto the same ordering even though it was refactored in this change, so anyone holding a valid GitHub authorization code can still drive unauthenticated User+Workspace row creation by replaying it with no `state` (10/min/IP throttle is the only limit). Pre-existing, but the change establishes the safer ordering next door and leaves this one behind.
searchedFor: read auth.controller.ts githubAuthCallback vs googleAuthCallback ordering

verdict.reason: The claimed absence holds in this repository. GitHubStrategy.validate (packages/backend/src/auth/github.strategy.ts:70-81) takes `emails?.[0]?.value` with no `verified` inspection and no rejection path (the file never imports UnauthorizedException), while UserService.findOrCreateUser (packages/backend/src/user/user.service.ts:40-48) resolves an account by `email` alone, ignoring the stored authProvider, and the GitHub callback passes the unchecked address straight in and mints a session (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:126-131, 225). The Google side does enforce verification (packages/backend/src/auth/google.strategy.ts:22-27, 81-86), so email is now a shared cross-provider identity guarded on only one side. I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: grep for verified/unverified/email_verified across packages/backend yields only google.strategy(.spec) plus unrelated hits; grep for `emails` across the backend hits only the two strategies and the endpoint-URL spec; grep for authProvider across packages/ shows no provider-match gate; there is no patches/ directory and no vendored or installed passport-github2 (glob **/node_modules/passport-github*/** returns nothing), so no in-tree library-level filter exists either. github.strategy.spec.ts asserts only endpoint URLs and state forwarding. The only possible mitigation lives in an external dependency whose behavior cannot be confirmed here, and GitHub's /user/emails is documented to return unverified addresses with a `verified` flag — resting an authentication boundary on that unverified assumption (and documenting it as safe in google.strategy.ts:19-20 and docs/design/backend.md:899-902) is itself the weakness. In-lane for the Security rubric (cross-provider account takeover / auth bypass), impact critical.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: isSecureCookie() (packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts:229-240) derives Secure/__Host- from COOKIE_SECURE, then GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL only (line 234), then NODE_ENV (239). GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL is never consulted anywhere in the file, yet oauth-providers.ts:18-22,38-40 makes it mandatory for Google precisely because Google requires an explicit redirect_uri, so it is an equally authoritative statement of the deployment's public scheme. The downgrade is reachable: github-auth.guard.ts:66-76 and packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:477-489 both document that an install with no GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL is a supported working deployment (GitHub falls back to the registered URL), and github.strategy.ts:46 passes it through with a bare non-null assertion without validation. Such an https install setting only GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL, no COOKIE_SECURE, and not running NODE_ENV=production falls to line 239 and issues the session (89-95), refresh, oauth-state (190), cli-state (141) and login-return cookies without Secure and without the __Host- prefix — the exact write restriction the module (26-47, 66-84) says is the only thing preventing sibling-subdomain cookie tossing of the double-submit secret and of wafflebase_session, i.e. session fixation, plus cleartext-transmissible session JWTs. No guard removes this: the only mitigation is Dockerfile:121 ENV NODE_ENV=production, which covers the shipped container only and not non-container installs. In-lane (auth/sensitive-data exposure), real, and fail-open, so it is not refutable on not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope grounds.
